avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, CNS signs, transverse myelitis on differential). In classic GBS it does not aid diagnosis.

specialized_test.impression: Acute demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy. Prolonged distal motor latencies bilaterally, reduced conduction velocities, partial motor conduction block at the fibular head, temporal dispersion. Absent or prolonged F-waves; H-reflex absent bilaterally. Sural-sparing sensory pattern. Findings are consistent with an acute demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy

patient.history_present_illness: A 19-year-old woman presents with one week of progressive limb weakness. Symptoms began with tingling in both feet and difficulty climbing stairs, and over seven days ascended to involve the thighs and then the hands, with mild distal numbness. She now cannot walk without assistance and struggles to rise from a chair. Three weeks ago she had community-acquired pneumonia, treated with a course of oral antibiotics and now fully resolved. Four days ago she received a seasonal influenza vaccine at a campus clinic. She reports no fever, no bladder or bowel dysfunction, no back pain, no diplopia, and no difficulty breathing or swallowing. There is no history of trauma, toxic ingestion, tick exposure, or recent travel. Her maternal grandmother has multiple sclerosis, but there is no family history of hereditary neuropathy. On examination she has symmetric flaccid weakness that is greater in the legs than the arms, mild distal sensory loss in a stocking-glove pattern, and global areflexia — absent reflexes in all four limbs are the critical finding pointing to an acute polyradiculoneuropathy rather than a myelopathy or a functional cause.

neurological_exam.additional: Bedside spirometry: forced vital capacity (FVC) 2.6 L (~70% predicted), single-breath count 28 — adequate but warrants serial monitoring. Community-acquired pneumonia 3 weeks ago, fully resolved. Received a seasonal influenza vaccine 4 days ago. No fever at presentation. No trauma, no toxic ingestion, no tick exposure, and no recent travel.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose intact in the arms; leg testing limited by weakness, with no cerebellar signs.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Normal. Extraocular movements full, pupils equal and reactive. No facial weakness, no ptosis. Bulbar function intact — normal speech and swallowing.
neurological_exam.gait: Unable to walk unassisted — requires support, with a steppage pattern from bilateral foot drop. Romberg deferred due to weakness.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and fully oriented. Anxious but cooperative. Speech fluent and normal.
neurological_exam.motor: Symmetric flaccid weakness, legs more than arms. Hip flexion 3/5 bilaterally, knee flexion/extension 4-/5, ankle dorsiflexion 3/5. Shoulder abduction 4/5, grip strength 4-/5 bilaterally. Tone reduced throughout. No fasciculations. Unable to rise from a chair without using the arms.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Global areflexia — biceps, triceps, brachioradialis, knee, and ankle jerks all absent bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor.
neurological_exam.sensory: Mild distal paresthesias in the feet and fingertips. Light touch and pinprick mildly reduced in a stocking distribution; vibration mildly reduced at the toes. No sensory level.
